stances.claim: Together with the Constitution, the Anti-Graft Law (RA 3019) and the Law of Forfeiture of Ill-Gotten Wealth (RA 1379), CJP considers the Ethical Standards Law (RA 6713) as the 'Bible' of public officials, who must therefore obey it -- especially amid these stupefying billion-peso pork barrel, trillion-peso legislative insertions, and other mind-bending scams. All these could have been prevented and the crooks penalized by its strict enforcement, especially by the Office of the Ombudsman (OMB) and the Civil Service Commission.
stances.rhetorical_move: Bible-titular characterization + four-pillar framework (Constitution + RA 3019 + RA 1379 + RA 6713) + scandal-timing anchoring + OMB-and-CSC enforcement charge

stances.claim: Sponsored by CJP's guru the late Senate President Jovito R. Salonga, the late Sen. Rene A. V. Saguisag, and others, the law was approved on Feb 20 1989; due to space limits, CJP will take up only (1) the norms of conduct and duties of public officials, (2) their prohibited acts and transactions, and (3) the penalties for the law's violations. Public officials under this and other laws 'include elective and appointive officials and employees, permanent or temporary, whether in the career or noncareer service, including military and police personnel, whether or not they receive compensation, regardless of amount.' They render public duties and use public funds.
stances.rhetorical_move: Salonga-and-Saguisag sponsorship credit + Feb-20-1989 approval anchor + three-part organizational structure + comprehensive-public-official verbatim-definition

stances.claim: Under norms and duties, public officials shall (a) always observe public interest over personal interest and use their powers 'efficiently, effectively, honestly and economically'; (b) act with justness and sincerity without discriminating against anyone 'especially the poor and underprivileged'; (c) not extend 'undue favors on account of their office to their relatives whether by consanguinity or affinity' except to their strictly confidential or coterminous staff; and (d) provide service without discrimination 'regardless of party affiliation or preference.'

Moreover, officials shall extend prompt + courteous + adequate service and 'provide information of their policies and procedures in clear and understandable language... ensure openness of information, public consultations, and hearings whenever appropriate, encourage suggestions, simplify, and systematize policy rules and procedures, avoid red tape...' Very importantly, public officials and 'their families shall live modest lives appropriate to their positions and income.'

Among other duties and obligations are to (a) respond, within 15 working days from receipt, to communications sent by the public with action-taken contained in the reply; (b) process documents and papers expeditiously, containing as far as practicable not more than three official signatures; (c) make documents accessible to and readily available for inspection by the public within reasonable working hours.

Public officials are barred from committing these prohibited acts -- (a) having directly or indirectly any financial or material interest in any transaction requiring their office's approval; (b) owning, controlling, managing, or accepting employment as officer/employee/consultant/counsel/broker/agent/trustee/nominee in any private enterprise regulated/supervised/licensed by their office unless expressly allowed by law; (c) engaging in private practice of their profession unless authorized by Constitution or law; or (d) recommending any person to any position in a private enterprise that has regular or pending official transactions with their office.

These prohibitions shall continue to apply for one year after resignation, retirement, or separation from public office, except in the case of professional private practitioners -- but the professional concerned cannot practice his/her profession in connection with any matter before the office he or she used to be with.
stances.rhetorical_move: one-year-post-separation continuation + professional-practice carve-out + can't-practice-before-former-office qualification

stances.claim: Public officials shall likewise submit SALNs and disclose their financial and business interests, including those of their spouses and of unmarried children under 18 living in their households. SALNs and disclosures must be filed (a) within 30 days after assumption of office; (b) on or before April 30 every year thereafter; and (c) within 30 days after separation from the service.
stances.rhetorical_move: SALN scope (self + spouse + minor-children-in-household) + three-stage timeline (30-days-after-assumption + April-30-annually + 30-days-after-separation)

stances.claim: In general, violations of RA 6713 shall be punished with a fine not exceeding six months' salary OR suspension not exceeding one year OR removal, depending on the gravity, after due notice and hearing by the appropriate body. However, criminal conviction of the prohibited acts and/or the failure to file SALNs and disclosures shall be more heavily punished -- imprisonment not exceeding five years, OR a fine not exceeding P5,000, OR both, AND/OR disqualification to hold public office.
stances.rhetorical_move: administrative-vs-criminal penalty taxonomy + due-notice-and-hearing procedural anchor

stances.claim: Any violation proven in a proper administrative proceeding by the OMB shall be sufficient cause for removal or dismissal, even if no criminal prosecution is instituted; private individuals who conspire with public officials shall be subject to the same penalties and tried jointly with them.

one_paragraph_summary: CJP characterizes RA 6713 (Ethical Standards Law) as the 'Bible' of public officials alongside the Constitution + Anti-Graft Law (RA 3019) + Law of Forfeiture of Ill-Gotten Wealth (RA 1379), arguing that the pork-barrel + trillion-peso-legislative-insertion + flood-control scams could have been prevented and the crooks penalized by its strict enforcement, especially by the OMB and Civil Service Commission. Crediting his guru the late Senate President Salonga and the late Sen. Saguisag as co-sponsors (Feb 20 1989 approval), he structures the column in three parts. On norms and duties: (a) public-interest-over-personal + efficient-effective-honest-economic, (b) just-and-sincere especially-for-the-poor, (c) no-undue-favors-to-relatives except strictly-confidential/coterminous staff, (d) no-discrimination-by-party-affiliation -- with the highlighted duty that officials and families 'shall live modest lives appropriate to their positions and income,' plus specific obligations (15-working-day response + three-signature processing + accessible documents). On prohibited acts: financial-interest-in-office-transactions + employment in regulated private enterprises + unauthorized private practice + recommendations to private enterprises with pending official transactions -- continuing for one year post-separation. SALNs must be filed within 30 days of assumption, annually by April 30, and within 30 days of separation, covering officials + spouses + unmarried minor children in household. Penalties graduate from administrative (fine/suspension/removal) to criminal (imprisonment ≤ 5 years + fine ≤ P5,000 + disqualification), with OMB administrative proceedings sufficient for removal even without criminal prosecution and private-individual conspirators tried jointly with public officials.
